I was recommended this place because I had heard great things about the staff and how well trained the veterinary team was. There were definitely a few employees who were absolute sweethearts and made the process of getting my dog neutered very easy. Unfortunately, my experience with the manager completely changed my overall impression of the place.

I understand that it is probably a very busy and stressful environment, but I still believe common courtesy and communication go a long way.

First, be aware that they may charge the card you used for your deposit for the remaining balance without telling you beforehand. I was never informed of this.

Second, make sure your dog does not eat or drink before the appointment. The booking process was very difficult and vague, and I don’t feel like their website clearly explains everything you need to know before the appointment.

The biggest issue, though, was the manager. I had arranged to pick my dog up early, but apparently her staff forgot to tell her. When I arrived, I was basically berated for being about 30 minutes early. If her own staff failed to communicate that with her, that is an internal communication issue. I should not have been made to feel like I did something wrong. I was also very uncomfortable with the way she spoke to her own employees in front of me.

What really upset me was how my dog was handled. He was extremely drowsy from surgery and could barely stand on his own. I specifically asked that he not be handled a certain way because I wanted to be extra careful with him. Despite that, the manager continued pulling on his collar and cone hard enough that he couldn’t stand properly and appeared to be choking. His poop bag holder also got caught between his collar and cone, which made the situation worse, and he eventually toppled over.

I also asked a question about my dog and was yelled at and told that she couldn’t tell me anything because she wasn’t trained to discuss it and that I shouldn’t have asked her. I understand that not everyone can answer medical questions, but there are respectful ways to communicate that.

At that point, one of the employees offered to bring my dog to my car. I told them, “You’ve done enough. I don’t appreciate the way you’ve spoken to me or the way you’ve handled my dog. We will patiently walk back to the car so he can regain himself. Do not lay another finger on him. If I have issues, I will go to someone who actually knows how to respect not only clients, but the animal too.” Then I walked out.

I want to be clear that several of the employees were incredibly kind and helpful, and I genuinely appreciate them. My issue is specifically with management and how this situation was handled.

I understand that mistakes happen and that working with animals can be stressful. I don’t expect perfection. I do expect basic communication, professionalism, compassion, and safe handling of my animal. Unfortunately, my experience with the manager did not meet those expectations.
